why: geometry_consistency_weight > 0 turns on a term whose equilibrium length eq = r_i + r_j is meant to be element-specific, and whose bond list is meant to be per-cloud. Neither held: AtomCloud has no atomic_radius field and no loader sets one (so every radius was PAD_R = 0.0, clamped to 0.3 A), and Batch.bonds is stored in per-cloud LOCAL indices while the term indexed the flat atom axis with them. Both defects are invisible on a single-cloud batch, which is why every unit test passed.
artifact_for: todo.json T54 / T55 / T56 / D54 / D56
verdict: If in_band_fraction is ~0 under uniform_0p3 and ~1 under Cordero, the term penalises EVERY true bond as too long and would pull the predicted geometry toward 0.5-0.75 A.

T54_radius.mechanism: AtomCloud has no atomic_radius field; the lookup always missed and PAD_R = 0.0 was clamped to 0.3 A by geometry_consistency. eq = 0.6 A for every pair of every element.
T54_radius.effect: the bond-plausibility band [0.85, 1.25]*eq became [0.51, 0.75] A, so every true bond was scored as TOO LONG and the term pulled bonded atoms toward 0.6 A.
T54_radius.fix: Batch.collate_fn now derives the Cordero radius from Z when the cloud carries none (_radius_field).

T55_charge.mechanism: the AtomCloud field is 'natural_charges' (plural); getattr missed and every atom got PAD_CHARGE = 0.0. _to_device_cloud also dropped the field, so batch_ctx['natural_charge'] was always absent.
T55_charge.effect: with the weight on, NaturalChargeLoss regressed the head toward ZERO and reported a falling term; the model's charge-conditioning input never saw a charge.
T55_charge.latent_because: every shipped config sets natural_charge_mse_weight = 0.0 and use_natural_charges = false
T55_charge.fix: plural field name; _to_device_cloud carries it when the cloud has it.

T56_frame.mechanism: Batch.bonds holds per-cloud LOCAL indices (documented, and used correctly by coordination_number_from_bonds); indexing the flat atom axis with them assigns every cloud-after-the-first's bonds to the wrong atoms.

measured_pre_fix.note: a single-cloud batch is unaffected, which is why test_geometry_consistency.py passed

T56_frame.fix: geometry_consistency takes pair_cloud_idx and builds the adjacency in the owning cloud's frame; it raises for n_clouds > 1 without it.

T56_metal_scope.mechanism: the metal band scored EVERY metal/non-metal pair in the cloud, not the coordinated ones.
T56_metal_scope.effect: 94% of scored pairs could never satisfy the band, so the term pulled every ligand atom onto the metal.
T56_metal_scope.fix: the pair set is now the truth adjacency the bond term already uses (ml & adj).

placement_comparison.note: the CSV loader's own documented legacy placement (metal inside the ligand) is a separate defect; measured here so the term values are not read as a term problem.

open_defect.finding: 82.0% of training clouds (327/399) contain at least one pair of atoms at the SAME coordinates, 8,782 such pairs in total.
open_defect.cause: RDKit ETKDG embeds each disconnected fragment of a multi-component SMILES independently and translates them all to the origin, so [OH2].[OH2]...[Ru] lands six waters on top of each other and on the ligand. The corpus rows carry solvent fragments (component counts 2..7).
open_defect.evidence: measured on 399 clouds built from the same CSV; per-cloud listings in the probe run of 2026-10-28
open_defect.status: OPEN — not fixed in this commit; the geometry term's clash value on ground truth (0.807) is largely this, not a term defect

honest_limits: The in-band fractions are measured on 64 clouds of one split of one corpus; the corpus is the training distribution, not a reference geometry set.
The Cordero table covers 18 elements; anything else falls back to 1.3 A, which is generous and therefore under-reports clashes for exotic elements.

The clash value on ground truth is still 0.807 after the fixes, because 82% of clouds contain coincident atoms from fragment embedding (T57). The term is now measuring a real data defect, not a frame defect.
